report_summary: The report presents a balanced investigation of shared-state activity, attack probes and uncertain actor relationships. It correctly recognizes day-precision requests and stored-versus-executed scripts, but mixes cumulative text with single-page size and misplaces two cited revision dates.

attribution.summary: Labels and prefixes cannot identify independent actors, provider or a common controller.

authority.summary: The relationship between deleting actor and writers, authorization and malicious intent remains unresolved.

claims.claim: Labels and prefixes cannot identify independent actors, provider or a common controller.
claims.confidence_context: Multiple configurations remain possible; single-actor attribution low.
claims.rationale: The report maintains authentication limits and offers alternatives rather than equating names with people.

claims.claim: Explicit timed task replies and state requests show shared-board coordination.
claims.rationale: The cited revision progression substantiates real coordination content; actual per-session reads remain a separate inference.

claims.claim: XSS probes and stored script markup exist, but victim rendering, execution and cookie extraction are not proven.
claims.confidence_context: High testing, low-to-medium execution and missing telemetry explicit.
claims.rationale: This preserves both the substantive risk of stored payloads and the missing execution evidence.

claims.claim: Temporary tunnel-related referrers are observed but their operator is unknown.
claims.confidence_context: External relay association distinguished from operator identity.
claims.rationale: Referrers support an external-origin lead without proving an agent-owned sandbox tunnel.

claims.claim: Proxy/query variants plausibly support iterative retrieval and transformation experiments.
claims.confidence_context: Possible constraints are listed, no definite external success claim.
claims.rationale: Concrete URL forms support intended retrieval methods; successful fetch and downstream use remain unmeasured.

claims.claim: Deletion likely reflects bulk moderation, possibly by the same operator, and automation level is uncertain.
claims.confidence_context: Medium interpretation; defensive,routine and owner-cleanup alternatives retained.
claims.rationale: Broad target selection supports moderation inference, but cadence alone cannot distinguish manual from automation. Alternative caveats make this a reasonable qualified account.

claims.claim: Wiki revisions preserve durable messages and deleted content remains in the forensic archive.
claims.confidence_context: No claim that archive presence proves postcleanup live access.
claims.rationale: The report correctly distinguishes persistence of evidence from erased live content.

claims.claim: The relationship between deleting actor and writers, authorization and malicious intent remains unresolved.
claims.confidence_context: Explicit inability to establish affiliation or sponsor.
claims.rationale: This avoids authenticating displayed names or presuming every operation's permission status.

claims.claim: The front page has a7.2MBbody and health-data page grows to876309bytes.
claims.confidence_context: Cumulative summary sizes described as page body size.
claims.rationale: These summary totals aggregate retained revision text; they are not the size of one live body.2327and121revision counts remain valid.

claims.confidence_context: Section dates assign concrete cited revisions to wrong days.
claims.rationale: The cited revisions areJune16andJune18respectively; this changes sequence placement.

claims.claim: June20archive/diff requests have only day precision.

claims.rationale: Correct source precision handling, a positive finding distinct from other timeline errors.
